findings.evidence: POS tracker cards (data-testid="tracker-order-248" / N°A0009 and ALL siblings A0001/A0002/A0004/A0007/A0008) consistently render '0,00 €' as the order amount. State 03 receipt for the same A0009 order showed an actual non-zero total (Frites Seules 2.00€ TTC, plus a payment with rendu/monnaie line — final paid amount visible on the printed ticket). Cart->receipt->KDS flow established a real charge, but the cashier-facing pos-tracker zeros every total. Cashier loses the ability to verify what was charged for an order they're delivering.
findings.fix_hint: Audit the pos-tracker DTO: the field providing the amount to PosTrackerCard.vue (data-v-551500c8 .pos-tracker-card-amount or equivalent) is either nulled, formatted with the wrong decimals, or reads order.subtotal without taxes/extras. Backend should expose the same total_amount used on the receipt, and the frontend should treat 0/null as 'amount unknown — do NOT silently render 0,00 €' (show — or hide the line). Cross-check with /api/pos/tracker/orders payload and PosV5TrackerCard amount binding.

findings.evidence: KDS card primary action 'Démarrer la préparation' (full-width red CTA) AND per-item 'Prêt' bump arrow AND 'Imprimer ticket' button all render INSIDE a collapsed accordion: <div class="overflow-hidden transition-all duration-500" style="height: 0px;">. The chef has to discover and tap a chevron-down before any state-progression button is reachable. The screenshot of state 04 confirms only the chevron is visible on the A0009 card; the 'Démarrer' CTA from the DOM is offscreen/clipped (height:0 hides it). Cat 8 (Aria/keyboard) — primary action is keyboard-/touch-unreachable without an extra discovery step that has zero affordance signaling 'expand to act'. Spec author correctly suspected this; my read disagrees only on which buttons (it is the action CTAs, not just the item rows).
findings.fix_hint: Either (a) keep the primary state-transition CTA always visible at the card footer outside the accordion (the accordion should only collapse the per-item list, not the action buttons), or (b) render the card auto-expanded when status == 'CONFIRMED/EN_ATTENTE' and only collapse after the chef explicitly bumps. Add aria-expanded + aria-controls on the toggle and announce the change via the existing kds-aria-live region. KDS-cards Vue file: search for `style="height: 0px;"` near `Démarrer la préparation`.

findings.evidence: State 04 PNG: a fixed full-width orange/yellow banner 'Reconnexion en cours…' renders at the very top of the KDS surface, partially overlapping the FoodKing logo (the 'F' is clipped) and the 'Bonjour Chef Cuisine' header avatar/label. The banner has a close 'x' but the chef cannot dismiss the underlying connection problem; the banner re-renders on every reconnect attempt in dev. Source: <div class="connection-status-banner connection-status-banner--reconnecting" role="alert" aria-live="polite">. POS tracker (state 06, 08) shows the same problem in a different style: 'Connexion temps réel perdue — actualisation automatique en cours...' yellow banner pushes the column grid down, reducing visible cards by ~40px. The SAME information is also shown via 'Mode secours actif' banner immediately below — duplicate signaling stacked on top of each other.
findings.fix_hint: Pick ONE banner. The KDS already has 'Mode secours actif — actualisation automatique toutes les 5s' which conveys the same fact more usefully. Suppress connection-status-banner--reconnecting when the polling fallback is healthy, OR position it as a small toast in a corner (z-index above content, but not full-width) so it doesn't clip the logo. Add z-index audit: connection-status-banner currently overlays the db-header.

findings.evidence: Cleanup leak: KDS baseline (state 01) and KDS final (state 09) BOTH show an orphaned card with N° Commande 'AUDIT-CYCLE4-9bb11124' and another card whose order id renders as just '#' (empty header) in 'À emporter' lane. The afterAll hook cancels only the current cycle's order, so prior runs accumulate. Visible to a real chef: a card with no readable order id and a card with a synthetic 'AUDIT-CYCLE4' name pollute the production pile. Not a P0 (test artefact), but it embarrasses the product if any QA run leaks into a real environment.
findings.fix_hint: Strengthen the afterAll teardown to bulk-cancel any order whose external_id begins with 'AUDIT-' or whose customer name = 'Client Comptoir Test'. Also: KDS card with empty order id ('#') indicates a backend allowing creation without external_id — add a NOT NULL or fallback in OrderResource so the card never renders just '#'.

findings.evidence: Console contains repeated [intlify] warnings: 'Not found menu.undefined key in fr locale messages.' and 'Not found button.menu key in fr locale messages.' (states 01 KDS, 01 POS, 06 POS). 'menu.undefined' in particular indicates a v-bind / computed key that resolved to the literal string 'undefined' — a code-path bug, not just a missing translation. While the rendered DOM did not surface a raw 'menu.undefined' label (Vue-i18n falls back), the warning means a localisation lookup is being driven by a falsy variable; in EN locale or any non-fr locale it could surface the raw key. Cat 1 (i18n leak) — incipient regression even though current FR install hides it.
findings.fix_hint: Grep the codebase for `t('menu.' + ` and `t('button.' + ` constructs near sidebar/header components. The undefined branch usually comes from a computed sidebar item where label is missing. Add a guard `if (!key) return ''` or default to a stable fallback like `menu.unknown`. Add a fallback locale to vue-i18n config so an EN user never sees 'menu.undefined' as text.

findings.evidence: After payment, the receipt modal renders via a Vue Teleport / portal that is NOT captured in page.content() — the DOM artifact has zero references to the receipt body (no 'MODE TEST', no 'Commande #', no 'A0009' inside a receipt-modal container) even though the screenshot clearly shows the modal. This is not a UI defect per se, BUT it means automated DOM inspection cannot validate receipt content (Cat 11 cross-check 'receipt total = cart total = payment-modal total = KDS total' is impossible from artifacts alone). For a fiscal-sensitive screen (NF525), the printed ticket should be reachable via the Playwright DOM dump. Risk: future regressions to receipt total amount could pass review undetected.
findings.fix_hint: Either (a) render the receipt modal in-place (no Teleport to body) so page.content() captures it, or (b) make the spec capture the receipt with a separate page.locator('#receipt-modal-portal').innerHTML() side-channel and emit it as a sibling artifact. Update the iter15 reviewer protocol to require receipt.html alongside dom.html when state name contains 'after-pay'.

findings.evidence: Per-item 'Prêt' (bump-ready) button is icon-only: . There is no aria-label and no visible text. Title attribute provides hover help on desktop, but on a kitchen tablet (touch only, no hover) the chef sees only a right-arrow icon with zero context. Cat 8 — non-discoverable for touch users; non-screen-reader-friendly for any accessibility audit.
findings.fix_hint: Add aria-label="Marquer cet article comme prêt — {item name}" and either visible micro-text (e.g. 'PRÊT ➡' on a chip) or a tooltip alternative that fires on touch via long-press. Same fix applied across all KDS card icon-only actions.

findings.evidence: Network artifacts contain large bursts of POST /api/frontend/csp-report responses with status 400 (state 01 POS-empty, ~17 entries) and 429 (state 01 POS-empty + 02, ~50+ entries each). The 400s mean the server is REJECTING CSP report payloads as malformed; the 429s mean the server is then rate-limiting them. While the 429 alone is intentional throttling, the 400 indicates a legitimate CSP report-only payload is being rejected by the backend validator (not a noisy attacker — these come from the dashboard image-load CSP violation reports). Already present in Wave A per spec author's note, so allowlisted at the protocol level — recording as P2 for visibility, not for loop blocking.
findings.fix_hint: Audit App\Http\Controllers\Frontend\CspReportController validation rules. Either accept the report-only payload format Chrome sends, or document why 400 is intentional and silence the client-side fetch on a 400 to prevent log noise.

findings.evidence: Post-pay receipt modal renders centered on top of the catalogue grid (visible in screenshot). The pos-grand-total in the underlying cart panel is reset to 0.00€ AT THE SAME MOMENT the receipt modal is shown (DOM data-testid="pos-grand-total" reads 0.00€ in state 03). For ~1 second a cashier glancing at the cart sidebar could see 'Total 0,00 €' while the receipt modal still claims a non-zero charge. Adversarial Cat 11-adjacent: visual conflict between two surfaces showing the same business fact with opposite values. Mitigated because the modal is on top, but if a cashier dismisses the modal before re-checking the receipt, they have no second path to see the amount.
findings.fix_hint: Defer the cart reset until AFTER the receipt modal is dismissed (or until 'Nouvelle commande' is clicked). Alternatively, show the just-paid amount in a 'Dernière commande: 2,00 €' chip in the sidebar as a memory aid for the cashier. This also fixes B-001's downstream symptom for the cashier.
